title: Norm Referencing vs. Criterion Referencing for AI Safety Thresholds

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Strong chain: regulators need absolute safety thresholds not relative rankings. Directly addresses the governance need for criterion-referenced standards with every link explicit.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Running benchmarks is straightforward, but defining criterion-referenced passing thresholds for safety properties requires domain expertise in what constitutes acceptable safety levels.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Scoping to one safety property is possible but defining passing criteria, running multiple models, and comparing scoring methods is sustained effort requiring careful design.

novelty.reasoning: While norm-referenced vs criterion-referenced assessment is well-established in education and the NIST AI RMF discusses risk tolerances, no published work was found that explicitly frames AI safety evaluation thresholds through the norm-referencing vs criterion-referencing lens. A grading rubric for AI safety frameworks exists (arxiv 2409.08751) but does not address this specific methodological distinction. The cross-disciplinary application to safety thresholds is novel.
